We need to find template that when applied to target molecule (the product) gives precursors matching DIBAL-H reduction of ester to aldehyde (or nitrile to aldehyde). The target molecule is given: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO . This appears to be a cyclic acetal? Actually contains a lactone? Let's see: It has a carbonyl CC=O (ketone) inside ring? The product after reduction of ester to aldehyde would have an aldehyde group. The target maybe the aldehyde product? The forward reaction: DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, breaking C-O bond (the O-alkyl) and reducing C=O from double to single (forming C-OH). So functional groups broken: carboxylic ester. Formed: aliphatic hydroxyls (primary alcohol). Also carbonyl becomes aldehyde (still carbonyl but order unchanged? Actually C=O remains double but changes from ester to aldehyde). But the description says bond order changes from 2 to 1 for C-O (the carbonyl O? Actually C=O to C-OH reduces order of C-O from double to single). So we need template that breaks an ester C-O bond and changes bond order.

We need to search template catalog with correct functional groups. Use get_available_functional_groups to see correct naming.
